reviewMethod: 16 timestamped RGB frames; motion not continuously viewed
limitations: Assistant visual screening of timestamped contact sheets, not a human annotation session, continuous playback or complete frame-by-frame video review.
Event intervals are provisional source-time approximations supported by sampled contact configurations. Continuity between frames, actual impacts and exact boundaries have not been verified.

Label 1 means selected staged physical-interaction imagery suitable for experimental positive training; it does not establish intent, injury, a crime or clinically/operationally validated violence recognition.
Only retained intervals are eligible. Initial approaches, separations and uncertain margins outside those intervals are not positive-labelled by this review.

Every retained interval spans at least two seconds and can cover the majority of a four-second training window. A four-second window must still be clipped to the source duration and checked for interval overlap.
All VID recordings and derivatives are training-only in this candidate. Actor/session lineage is unknown, so no VID calibration or unseen evaluation claim is supported.
Scene groups refer only to visible backgrounds and conservatively similar locations. They neither identify actors nor establish distinct recording sessions.
Ambiguous and excluded recordings have no accepted positive intervals. Unreviewed recordings remain excluded from the candidate manifest.

recordings.notes: Three people approach, turn and make intermittent arm/shoulder contact among classroom chairs. Sparse frames do not separate brief directed actions from ordinary positioning or establish a clear sustained contact episode. Publisher class alone is insufficient.

Repeated sampled views show a standing person leaning over and gripping the upper body of a seated person, with substantial sideways chair/body displacement. Retain the central contact span; omit the early setup and late release. Continuity and force are not independently measured.

Separated figures make raised-arm and leg movements near an entrance; a long light-coloured prop is visible in later frames. No sufficiently clear sustained person-to-person contact interval can be assigned from these samples. Do not train the prop or raised-arm appearance as a positive shortcut.

Across the retained central frames a standing person maintains an upper-body grip on a seated/crouched person while their torsos repeatedly bend and move together. Other people are present. The interval is a provisional subset of the longer interaction; omit the initial approach and final hand-obstructed margin.

Two central people repeatedly hold/contact each other's upper arms and shoulders while turning and bracing, visible across adjacent sampled frames. Retain the central paired contact configurations; omit the early approach and final edge of the clip. No specific strike, intent or injury is established.

Two central people remain closely joined at shoulders/upper arms through the retained samples, with repeated bent torsos, pulling-like arm configurations and shared rotation. Retain only the sustained close-contact portion; surrounding observers do not supply additional positive events.

The central people are repeatedly joined through arms/shoulders while one torso bends and rotates; another person remains very close. Multiple samples support a contact episode, although precise impacts cannot be established. Exclude the initial uncertain margin and the visibly separating final frames.

Several people are spaced around the atrium making large arm movements with long light-coloured props. The samples do not establish a clear sustained unarmed body-contact interval. Exclude rather than learn props, gestures or the publisher label as evidence of the target interaction.

Brief arm/shoulder contacts alternate with separation and large gestures among three figures. The clearly supported contact bursts are too short or interrupted to assign a conservative two-second interval from these frames. Continuous playback could resolve the ambiguity; it was not performed.

A rear figure maintains shoulder/upper-torso contact with the central figure across the retained samples while the central figure repeatedly lifts a leg toward the person in front. Positive support is the sustained upper-body hold and combined physical interaction; actual kicks or impacts are not asserted. Initial and final margins are omitted.

Wide distant view shows several separated figures making large gestures, with prop-like thin objects visible. Clear prolonged body contact cannot be resolved at this scale. Exclude instead of assigning the full clip positive from its folder name.

Two people repeatedly extend arms near one another while a third stands behind. Sampled hand/forearm proximity is insufficient to distinguish brief contact from ordinary greeting or gestures, and no sustained upper-body hold is clear. No positive interval retained.

Two close figures repeatedly maintain shoulder/head-area and upper-arm contact while bending and rotating together across the central samples. Retain that paired contact span; exclude the approach/start edge and later release/bent-away frames. Hand placement does not establish choking or injury.

Several figures make arm extensions near the entrance. A possible rear upper-body hold is partly obscured, and foreground approaches/retreats interrupt the visible contact evidence. The sampled frames do not support a sufficiently certain sustained interval; exclude from positive training pending better temporal review.

The two figures become small and partly obscured near a distant doorway. Sixteen frames across almost nineteen seconds leave more than a second between observations. Arm proximity and body positioning cannot establish a conservative continuous contact interval; do not interpolate a long positive episode.

Two central people repeatedly hold/contact shoulders and upper arms while bending and turning together, including a clearly bent torso in the middle of the sequence. Keep the sustained paired-contact subset and omit the less certain initial and separating final margins. Continuous motion was not viewed.

One figure repeatedly raises and extends an arm toward another, but the figures remain separated in several samples. Brief possible contacts and large temporal sampling gaps do not establish a two-second sustained episode. Do not turn arm-raising alone into a positive label.

People remain distributed across a wide outdoor view with repeated large gestures and prop-like objects. No conservative sustained body-contact interval is visually resolved; reject as a positive training example in this selection.
